nomenclature.etymology_html:
-Alangium : From a Malayalam vernacular name, alangi, used in Kerala (Southwestern India) for the plant.
-Salviifolium : From the Latin salvia-folium meaning "sage-leaved".

stem_bark.text: The bark of Alangium salviifolium is rough, grey-coloured and longitudinally fissured.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Alangium salviifolium is rough, grey-coloured and longitudinally fissured.

fruit.text: The fruit of Alangium salviifolium is an ellipsoid drupe . It is about 2 cm long and 1 cm wide, pubescent and purple-coloured when ripe. The fruit contains one seed.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Alangium salviifolium is an ellipsoid drupe. It is about 2 cm long and 1 cm wide, pubescent and purple-coloured when ripe. The fruit contains one seed.

flower.text: The flowers of Alangium salviifolium are grouped in short axillary cymes. The flowers are 5-merous. The calyx-tube is urn-shaped, 1-2 mm long with triangular lobes up to 1.5 mm long. The calyx is light green and tomentose. The corolla is composed of 10 cream-coloured,reflexed and strap-shaped petals. The petals are densely tomentose outside and glabrous inside, 1-1.5 cm long and 2 mm wide. The androecium is composed of 10-30 stamens. The filaments are 5-10 mm long. The style is 1.5-2 cm long style with a capitate stigma at the end. The ovary is turbinate and 1-celled. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:

leaf.text: The leaves of Alangium salviifolium grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is chartaceous and glabrous on both sides (pubescent on the veins on both sides). The leaves have a 1 cm long petiole . The leaf of Alangium salviifolium is 10-15 cm long and 3-4 cm wide. The shape of the blade is lanceolate, the apex is acute, the base is rounded and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Alangium salviifolium is a medium-sized, thornless and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.
habit.text_html: Alangium salviifolium is a medium-sized, thornless and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.

ecology.text: Alangium salviifolium is usually found near sandy riverine tracts, by the side of roads, on tank bunds, or on agricultural boundaries.
ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Alangium salviifolium is usually found near sandy riverine tracts, by the side of roads, on tank bunds, or on agricultural boundaries.

distribution.text: Southern and Eastern Asia, tropical Australia, western Pacific Ocean islands and New Caledonia, western Africa and Madagascar.
distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :

    Southern and Eastern Asia, tropical Australia, western Pacific Ocean islands and New Caledonia, western Africa and Madagascar.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Alangium salviifolium is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Alangium salviifolium is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Alangium salviifolium are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Alangium salviifolium is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Alangium salviifolium is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Alangium salviifolium are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.

others.text: The twigs are used for brushing the teeth in India. A mixture of mature fruits of Alangium salviifolium with honey and rootstocks of sweet flag ( Acorus calamus ) is used to manage pests on agricultural crops. Source : Ebanyenle, E., 2009. handicrafts.text: The wood of Alangium salviifolium is valued for musical instruments and furniture. It is used in building as beams, for flooring, furniture, cabinet work, inlaying, carving, bobbins, spindles, shuttles, rice pestles, tool handles, walking sticks, gunstocks and handicraft articles. Source : Ebanyenle, E., 2009. Alangium salviifolium (L.f.) Wangerin. In: Lemmens, R.H.M.J., Louppe, D. & Oteng-Amoako, A.A. (Editors). Prota 7(2): Timbers-Bois d'oeuvre. PROTA, Wageningen, Netherlands.

medicinal.text: The leaves are used to cure asthma and as cataplasm to reduce rheumatic pains. The fruit is cooling, tonic, nutritive, useful in burning of the body, consumption, and in haemorrhage. The fruit is used as purgative, expectorant, carminative and as an antidote for poisoning. It was also used in leprosy. The fruit juice is applied to cure eye diseases. The stem is used to cure diarrhoea and vomiting. The roots and the fruits are used for the treatment of rheumatism and haemorrhoid. The root bark is also used in skin problems and as an antidote for snake bite. It is also used to expel parasitic worms and other internal parasites from the body. It is also used as an emetic and purgative. Sources : - Basu & Kirtikar, 1918, Indian Medicinal Plants - Ebanyenle, E., 2009. Alangium salviifolium (L.f.) Wangerin. In: Lemmens, R.H.M.J., Louppe, D. & Oteng-Amoako, A.A. (Editors). Prota 7(2): Timbers-Bois d'oeuvre. PROTA, Wageningen, Netherlands.

reforestation.text: Alangium salviifolium is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Alangium salviifolium is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
